lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Have you tried heading in the direction the transport ship comes from?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Yes, but without any luck.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: There's no way to determine where it comes from.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Sounds like optical camouflage... Didn't the Ark lose that technology?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: They can use what they still have, though.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: The fact that they're going through the trouble to use optical camouflage means they're trying to keep this insane experiment a secret...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: What in the world could they gain by doing this over and over?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Who knows. I'll never understand what those buffoons in the Ark think.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Well, then let's find out.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Chatterbox. You have a corruption generator, don't you?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: In that case, when the next human imposter arrives...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Actually, no. That wouldn't be wise.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: You're unique in more than one way. There's nothing to be gained from you revealing yourself.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: If there's a Black Smith nearby, bring it here.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: We can use it to apply the corruption, and then check on the results.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: If the corruption takes hold successfully, have some nearby Raptures bring our subject over here.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Make sure you don't go even remotely close to that site yourself.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: You're being extremely cautious.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: There's nothing wrong with being careful.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: So what do you say?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: ... I'll do it.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Good. In the meantime, let's have fun waiting.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I can't wait to know what's inside that weird human imposter's head.
A Maria-n lies collapsed. Her eyes are red, and she keeps repeating the same words over and over.
There are two tubes driven into her head.
Apart from her arms and legs twitching on occasion, she doesn't move at all.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: What the...?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Did you find something?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: She has an inexplicable amount of combat experience.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: So she's a veteran.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: No, she's far beyond that.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: The number of battles she's fought is at least one... actually, two orders of magnitude greater than the Goddess Squad.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Her body's specs are also extraordinary... In fact, they're vastly superior to any other human imposter.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: The problem is... she has no talent. Her rate of victory is abysmal.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: She has essentially just... fought a lot of battles.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: ... But she really has fought a lot of battles...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: How is this even possible?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Chatterbox, could you have the next imposter corrupted as well?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Then bring her to me.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: If you intend on giving orders, it's only polite to share what you've learned.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I'm not certain yet. I think I'll know after the next one, so I'll tell you then.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Hmm. Very well.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Ah, I died. Ah, I died. Ah, I died. Ah, I died.
Another Maria-n's eyes are red, and she keeps repeating the same words over and over.
There are two tubes driven into her head.
Mirror peers at her for a long while, then bursts out laughing.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Heheh... Hahaha...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Hahahaha!

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Did something break inside of you?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Haha... ha...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Heh... They're insane.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I know we're not ones to talk, but they do not seem to have any regard for life.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: That kind of makes me like them.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: I think a little explanation is in order, don't you?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Take this one to the Lift, Chatterbox.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I'm going to try turning her into an elite... or a Heretic, as the Ark calls them.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Again? How many times is this now?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Just think, though: if we take such an abnormal imposter and turn her into a Heretic...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: aren't you curious to see what she turns out like?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: I've kept quiet up until now, but I can't let you create any more elites without the Queen's permission.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: What...? And who are you to say no?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Would you please kindly do as you're told?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: After all, I'm the one who put you on the Raptures' side. Kindness should be met with kindness.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I'll even allow you to watch how a Heretic is made just this once. I have a good feeling about this one.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: I'll go on ahead. Do hurry.
Mirror vanishes in a burst of static.
Chatterbox looks at the Maria-n. Her eyes glow red as she twitches.
He grips her torso in his hand and moves out.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: ... Hmph.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Ahhhhh!
A scream.
*Clank, clank, clank*
The loud clang of steel.
*Bzzzzz*
The sound of something being cut and gouged.
*Glug, glug, glug*
The sound of something being injected.
*Splash*
The sound of something spilling out.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Aaahhhhh!
An even louder scream.
*Crack, snap!*
The sound of something being torn and pierced.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Ooh, it's working. Usually it stops partway through.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: ... So this is how a Heretic is made.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Yes. Not so different from making a human imposter, is it?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: You take corrupted NIMPH and extract from it its ideal form—as a Rapture, that is—to use as a base.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Then, the many nanomachines put inside the body will construct a new body.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Granted, the process can be painful, as the original body is ripped apart, pierced, and melted to form the new body.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: What's the success rate?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: The more extraordinary the subject's abilities, the greater the odds.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: This human imposter's NIMPH is not ordinary, so the body should at least fully form.
*Crack, snap!*

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Aaahhhhh!

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Hehe. I can't wait to see the results.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: Can I become a Heretic too?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Is being a casualty of that idiotic male Nikke project not enough for you?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: You were discarded as a failure by the Ark. Do you want the Raptures to discard you as well?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Don't ask for too much, Chatterbox.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: The Queen dislikes those who are greedy.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: ... I see. I'll keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Oh, it looks like the process finished while we were chitchatting.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: But...
*Crack, crack*

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Agh... Eeeah...
What had been a Maria-n is now an unrecognizable mass.
An outer skin covered in irregular lumps, an unidentifiable liquid that seems to boil, and organs in places they shouldn't be.
Red eyes, and a mouth-like organ that is opening and closing.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Egh... Augh... Ayeck...

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: A splendid Heretic.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Hmm. This one's no good.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: It technically is a Heretic, but in this state...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Chatterbox, go ahead and dispose of...

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: ... Is this...?
Mirror stares at a part of the mass.
Her eyes widen.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: ... A gene...?

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Why would it be in something this... formless...?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: It has far too many memories for any single entity.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: And something like that counts as immense power in the eyes of the Seven Arbiters...?

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Haha... I don't know whether to call that a generous take, or a stupid one.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: What are you talking about? Explain.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: You should get away from here, Chatterbox. As fast as you can.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: If you don't want to be found, that is.

lines.speaker: talkative
lines.text: I told you to explain.

lines.speaker: mirror_r
lines.text: Fine, you can stay here and find out. It was fun while it lasted.
Mirror vanishes in a burst of static.
Chatterbox lets out rough, growling breaths for a moment before also leaving.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Ugh... agh... eck...
The mass twitches alone in the dark space.
A moment later, the wall of the Lift is pierced through,
as a ferocious jet of water shoots through the mass,
killing it in an instant.
The Gene Reaper watches it for a moment with emotionless eyes,
then flies off elsewhere.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Argh!
Doctor Maria slams the desk.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Corrupted, corrupted, corrupted! And corrupted again! How many times is this now?!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: And why do they keep getting corrupted?! What changed?

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Doctor?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You... Stop getting corrupted.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Oh, right... The moment you're corrupted, the data stops updating.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You wouldn't remember.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Are you all right? If there's anything I can do to help...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: No, never mind. Just hurry up and get ready to go.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Doctor, maybe you should rest...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: There's no time. We have to make as much progress as we can...

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Sure, but you haven't slept at all lately.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: I'll work even harder, so please, at least have a short nap...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: How about instead of wasting time worrying about me, you come up with ways to make progress!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You're not getting better at all! You just keep dying, without any sign of improvement!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: At this rate, I'll...!

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Please...! I'm begging you! Produce some sort of tangible result...! That's all I'm asking...!

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: Okay, Doctor.

lines.speaker: maria-n
lines.text: I'll produce results.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... Good. I'm counting on you.
Maria-n walks off, listless.
Doctor Maria doesn't even look at her, but keeps her eyes glued to the monitor.
Maria-n steps off the transport ship.
She looks at the surface stretching out before her.
I'm tired of this.
I'm scared.
I'm both sick and scared of dying.
It's pointless. How much longer do "I" have to keep doing this?
Is there really an end to this? And if we reach it, what will happen to "me"?
I'm sure "I" will just be thrown onto the battlefield and repeat all of this again.
I'm tired of it. I'm scared.
It feels like I'm about to fall apart.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Once again, it's nice to meet you, Maria-2.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: From now on, you and I are going to... um...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: work together to bring victory to humanity.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I have high expectations of you.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: B-but of course, I won't just dump everything on you. I'll be working hard too.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: ... Hm? Your name?

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Oh... Well, I made you based on myself, so that's just how I named you.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: I figured it'd be confusing if we had the exact same name, though, so you became Maria-2.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Why not start from 1? I guess because 1 is... me, haha.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Hm... Is that a little too lazy? Maybe it'd be better to give you a different...

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Oh, you like it? Good, I'm glad to hear it.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: Well, again, I look forward to working with you, Maria-2.

lines.speaker: doctormaria
lines.text: You and I now share the same fate.
Hers was the first face I saw after I was made.
The first voice I heard.
The first warmth I felt.
Those were the only good things "I" knew, so they were the only things I sought after.
But...
Now I'm lonely.
There is no more kindness in those eyes anymore.
No more warmth in her words.
They've been replaced with resentful words, and glaring eyes.
That is all "I" have anymore.
The only thing "I" can do is die, and die, and die again,
and even those deaths are meaningless.
Now "my" very existence means nothing. I am nothing, not even worth counting.
Still, despite all that, the reason I can keep going is...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Hi!

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Wow, you're the first kid my age I've seen here.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: What's your name?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: {AccountData.NickName}? Haha, that's a weird name.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: How'd you end up in here?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: You're sick? Well yeah, I figured that, since this is a hospital.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I'm sick too. They said it's... I can't remember. Something to do with my brain.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Oh, I haven't even introduced myself.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: You can call me...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Maria. My name's Maria.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: So, {AccountData.NickName}... do you wanna be friends?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I hate how quiet it is here. It's all old people.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: We should talk and play together. See, I'm not allowed to go outside.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Huh? You can't either?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Perfect. Wanna play a word game together?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: You don't know any word games? That's okay. I'll teach you.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Do you not have a mom or dad?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Oh. That's okay. I don't have a dad either.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: And my mom... I haven't seen her in a long time.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: She says she's super busy chasing her dream.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: She won't tell me what her dream is, though.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: What's so good about dreams, anyway? I don't really get it.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Oh, do you have a dream? What is it?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... You want to be a commander?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Why would you wanna be something like that?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I heard they don't make much money, and it's really dangerous.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Also, isn't their average lifespan only like thirty years? It's really short, anyway.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: And yet, you still want to be a commander?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Haha! Oh really?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: That's quite the dream. Are you sure it's not a little too big?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Well, I'll root for you anyway. And your dream.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: If...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: And this is a big if...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: If I ever become a Nikke...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I hope you'll be my Commander.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: D-don't come any closer...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I'm hurt...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I'm all sweaty too... and I smell bad...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I-I said don't come closer...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: You dummy. What are you bandaging it for?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Because the bandage will help it heal faster? That's true, but... my head...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... No. Thank you.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Yeah. I'm okay. It doesn't hurt now.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... You're really nice.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... Does it hurt a lot?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: I can tell you're not okay. Don't lie.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Yeah, I'm here. I'm not going anywhere until you feel better.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... Oh, I have an idea.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: If I do... this, and then...

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Wh-why are you laughing? You're the one who said bandages make things better.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: D-don't laugh!

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... Hey, {AccountData.NickName}. Are you dying?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Don't die.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Whoa, what's this? A flower?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Where'd you get it? Huh? You made it?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Oh, this is a bandage, huh? Haha! You made a flower out of a bandage?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: That's amazing. I had no idea you could make this sort of thing.

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... It's for me?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: Wh-why?

lines.speaker: girl
lines.text: ... You dummy.
He was a beam of sunshine.
He helped me endure that terrible loneliness.
I don't even know when it's from,
but that vague fragment of a memory,
that tiny speck of a memory buried among countless others,
while certainly not much,
is what allows "me" to dream about the future.
A future where, someday, we will meet again.
